title: Some people earn a lot but aren’t rich

paragraphs: About 14% of US households earn over 200,000 dollars annually, but many high earners don’t feel rich. These individuals are called HENRYs—High Earners, Not Rich Yet.

Even people making over 300,000 often struggle with credit card debt. This is partly due to lifestyle creep, where people increase their spending as their income rises. Many HENRYs live in high-cost cities and have growing expenses like rent, food delivery, and subscriptions. They compare themselves to others in their income group, making them feel financially behind.

Experts say budgeting, knowing your net worth, and planning for savings are key steps to feeling financially secure. While earning more can offer freedom, it doesn’t always reduce stress. Emotional spending, social pressure, and a lack of financial planning can keep high earners stuck on a hamster wheel, always working but never feeling financially safe or satisfied.

everything you own minus everything you owe
a cycle where you keep working but don’t feel progress

paragraphs: Many people in the US make over 200,000 dollars a year, but they still don’t feel rich. These people are called HENRYs, which means High Earners, Not Rich Yet.

Even people who make 300,000 dollars a year have money problems and debts. They make more money, but they also spend more. This is called lifestyle creep. They buy more food, rent expensive homes, and want to live like their friends. They don’t always save enough money. Living in cities like New York or Los Angeles costs more, too.

Even with high pay, people feel like they must keep working all the time. Experts say it is important to make a budget and know your net worth, which is what you own minus what you owe. That helps people plan and save for the future.

words.d: money you owe and must pay back
a plan for how to spend money
when you must give back something someone gave you

paragraphs: Some Americans make a lot of money, but they do not feel rich. They are called HENRYs. This means High Earners, Not Rich Yet.

Even people who make 300,000 dollars a year can have problems with money. They earn more, but they spend more too. This is called lifestyle creep. They spend more on food, rent, and fun. They also feel that they must have the same things as their friends. Many rich people live in big cities where everything is more expensive.
Experts say that people should make a plan and save money. They need to know how much money they have and how much they owe. It helps them feel better about money and the future.

words.d: when you have a lot of money
when you must give back what you have from someone else
